title: Хочешь здесь жить – выращивай еду: необычное правило действует в районе возле Амстердама
content:
Тем, кто не готов обрабатывать землю или проводить время на природе, будет непросто адаптироваться к жизни в общине Остерволд в Нидерландах. Здесь жители должны использовать не менее половины своей собственности для сельского хозяйства.
Как пишет antena3.ro, Остерволд – это городской эксперимент, занимающий примерно 4300 гектаров в восточной части города Алмере, недалеко от Амстердама. Проект был задуман более десяти лет назад и разработан местными властями совместно с градостроителями.
По меньшей мере половина каждого участка должна использоваться для выращивания продуктов питания. С помощью этого правила власти надеются сделать территорию более устойчивой и сохранить ее сельский характер.
Свобода, но и обязательства
Тот, кто покупает и застраивает участок земли, также должен внести свой вклад в создание необходимой инфраструктуры. Жители заботятся о дорожной части, относящейся к их собственности, энергоснабжении, канализации, сборе мусора, зеленых насаждениях и городском сельском хозяйстве. Эти работы могут выполняться индивидуально или совместно с другими членами сообщества.
Для сохранения сельского облика района генеральный план предусматривает, что 18% территории должно быть занято зданиями, 8% – дорогами, 13% – общественными зелеными зонами, 2% – водными ресурсами и 59% – городским сельским хозяйством.
Правила допускают широкий спектр проектов: жилье вокруг полей для гольфа, плантации, самодостаточные виллы или небольшие сообщества, создаваемые группами собственников.
Люди, не умеющие обрабатывать свою землю, могут нанять "городского фермера". Специальная платформа связывает землевладельцев с людьми, имеющими опыт в сельском хозяйстве.
Конечная цель – обеспечить производство в Остерволде 10% продуктов питания, потребляемых в Алмере. При этом Остерволд предоставляет жителям большую свободу в выборе способов обработки своей земли. У некоторых есть фруктовые сады, другие используют теплицы или создают небольшие пастбища. Каждый владелец может придумать свои собственные идеи и методы.
Ранее мы рассказывали, как австралийская семья приобрела остров, чтобы заниматься овцеводством. Теперь они отказались от фермерства и совместно с государством превращают эту территорию в безопасное убежище для исчезающих видов животных.

title: Delcy Rodríguez entregó 48 viviendas en Ciudad Tiuna a familias afectadas por los terremotos
content:
La presidenta encargada de Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, encabezó este lunes el acto de entrega de 48 apartamentos en el sector Simón Bolívar del Complejo Habitacional Ciudad Tiuna, en Caracas, como parte del plan de atención integral desplegado tras los terremotos el 24 de junio.
La jornada beneficia directamente a 177 personas pertenecientes a 48 núcleos familiares que sufrieron daños en sus inmuebles y que habían sido resguardadas en campamentos transitorios.
La adjudicación constituye la tercera fase de entregas en el desarrollo urbano de Fuerte Tiuna, alcanzando acumulado de 287 viviendas otorgadas en ese sector para el resguardo de 897 habitantes.
Con esta entrega, la gestión gubernamental contabiliza 335 viviendas asignadas como parte de la meta nacional que contempla la construcción y entrega de 4.000 hogares antes de finalizar diciembre de 2026.
Para cumplir con la reubicación de quienes permanecen en refugios temporales, el gobierno interino anuncia además un plan complementario que abarca la adquisición de inmuebles en el mercado secundario, esquemas de alquiler garantizado y la rehabilitación de más de 13.000 casas, medida con la que se proyecta llegar a cerca de 66.000 ciudadanos.
Los balances de la Comisión Presidencial reflejan el avance en la inspección técnica de 59.000 estructuras en la Región Capital.
De este universo evaluado, 10.332 inmuebles fueron clasificados bajo la etiqueta roja de riesgo inminente, por lo que requerirán estudios especializados de ingeniería para determinar su viabilidad estructural o su demolición.

title: Heat-pump water heaters just keep getting better
content:
Next Upcoming
Rural America & The Clean Energy Transition at Climate Week NYC
By Canary Media
Last November, Jonathan Cohen needed a new water heater for the house he and his wife had recently purchased.
The labor economist at Amazon was keen to get a heat-pump water heater, a superefficient electric technology that could save him money on his utility bills. Thorough by nature, he emailed 12 plumbers to ask how much it would cost to install Wirecutter’s top pick. He got few responses, none encouraging. Plumbers who were willing to install that model said the price would depend on an unknown quantity: subcontracted electrical work.
Cohen recoiled at the potential logistical nightmare. “You’re dealing with a plumber, and then they have to coordinate with an electrician, and they have to get separate quotes and pull the permits,” he explained. “I didn’t want to be a project manager.”
Then his brother-in-law told him about Reservoir, a new heat-pump water heater startup that has in-house tradespeople and competitive pricing that includes installation.
Cohen loved the idea of such a frictionless process, he said, as he walked around his Somerville, Massachusetts, neighborhood with a 6-month-old strapped to his chest. “They definitely catered to me.” In late 2025, Cohen had a Reservoir unit installed that cost him a little over $4,000 after federal and local incentives.
The Boston-based startup made a splash earlier this month when it announced it had raised $8 million in seed funding to grow beyond its roughly 100 local installations. And it’s just one of several companies offering new innovations to attract consumers to the climate-friendly appliance.
Heat-pump water heaters are about three times as efficient as gas-fired or electric-resistance varieties, cut planet-warming emissions, and often lower monthly utility bills. Switching from a resistance system can save a household almost $23,000 over the appliance’s 15-year lifetime. Because they move heat instead of generating it, heat-pump water heaters act like air conditioners and can replace dehumidifiers, saving homes with muggy basements hundreds of dollars each summer.
But the tech has yet to take off. While Americans bought 5 million electric water heaters in 2025, beating out the next most-popular option, gas-fired, only an estimated 214,000 were heat-pump water heaters, according to the decarbonization nonprofit New Buildings Institute.
“The biggest barrier is cost,” said Noah Gabriel, senior project manager at the institute. Consider the difference in two products from leading manufacturer Rheem: A 50-gallon heat-pump water heater has a list price of $1,699, while a highly rated electric-resistance model retails for just $799. The installation cost for a heat-pump version can be comparable to that for conventional systems, adding another $1,000 to $4,000 or more, depending on factors like tank size, a home’s electrical readiness, and local labor costs.
President Donald Trump and the Republican-led Congress have made transitioning to heat-pump water heaters more expensive. Last year, they eliminated a Biden-era federal tax credit that offered households a discount of up $2,000 on the appliance.
Some states, cities, and utilities continue to offer rebates on heat-pump water heaters — from $150 to a whopping $4,000. Meanwhile, though, manufacturers have been coming out with new models and features that could help make their products more affordable.
Although heat-pump water heaters typically plug into a 240-volt outlet, a few big brands — Rheem, A.O. Smith, and GE Appliances — now produce versions that conveniently use a normal 120-volt socket. They’re less powerful, but these options can work well for households of one to four people that would otherwise have to upgrade their electrical system. Last year, GE became the first to offer a product with a flexible voltage, which experts say could make emergency replacements much easier.
While most heat-pump water heaters need 400 to 700 cubic feet of air around them from which to pull heat and put in the tank, customers with tighter spaces can use what are known as split systems. These models move the heat-pump half of the water heater outdoors and leave the hot water tank indoors. Manufacturer SanCO2 has sold such a product for years, and this April, A. O. Smith came out with its own offering. This month, Midea won a national competition for its split-system prototype.
To help users save money more aggressively, most manufacturers have created apps so that households can schedule their heat-pump water heaters to use grid power when it’s cheapest. The appliances can also be set up to participate in local utility programs, like California’s WatterSaver, that reward customers for turning down energy use when the grid is stressed, according to Gabriel. However, some users have reported glitches with some of these scheduling systems.
To reduce the onus on customers, Reservoir and startup Cala Systems are embedding their products with onboard computers to automatically take advantage of cheap power. Each company’s software also learns how much hot water you need daily, and at what times, in order to deliver hot showers with minimal energy use. Most heat-pump water heaters have backup electric-resistance elements to heat water in a flash, but it’s much more efficient to run the heat pump slowly and steadily over a few hours. Cala Systems, which has sold nearly 400 units across 36 states, says it’s been able to reduce use of the backup element from the typical 35% of the appliance’s energy use to just 7%.
As for Cohen, he’s become something of an evangelist for his heat-pump water heater, recommending it to friends who have just bought their own homes.
While Cohen’s basement used to have a whiff of gas, his Reservoir water heater lets him breathe easier, he said. “It’s really nicely designed.”

title: Ugunduzi muhimu na wa kushangaza zaidi wa 2025
content:
Ugunduzi muhimu na wa kushangaza zaidi wa 2025
Ugunduzi wa kisayansi ni matokeo mapya yanayobadilisha jinsi tunavyoelewa ulimwengu. Hutokea kupitia tafiti za kisayansi, fikra, au wakati mwingine bahati tu.
Kwa mazuri au mabaya, hizi hapa gunduzi saba ambazo ni mafanikio ya mwaka 2025 na zimebadilisha maisha yetu.
Kompyuta yenye kasi zaidi duniani
Januari, kompyuta yenye kasi zaidi duniani ilizinduliwa katika Maabara ya Kitaifa ya Lawrence Livermore huko California. Inaitwa El Capita, ni kompyuta ya tatu ya aina hiyo, ambapo Inaweza kufanya hesabu za 1.8 kwantilioni kila sekunde.
Kama kila mtu Duniani angekuwa na kikokotoo na kufanya kazi saa 24 kwa siku, siku 7 kwa wiki, akifanya hesabu moja kwa kila sekunde, itamchukua binadamu zaidi ya miaka bilioni kadhaa kumaliza idadi ya hesabu ambazo El Capitan hukamilisha kwa sekunde moja tu.
Kompyuta yako ya kawaida ya mkononi inaweza kufanya hesabu bilioni kadhaa kwa sekunde. El Capitan ina kasi ya takriban mara milioni moja kuliko kompyuta yako ya nyumban
Kompyuta hiyo kubwa itatumika kupanga akiba ya silaha za nyuklia ya Marekani na kutafiti muundo wa silaha mpya. Ujenzi wake ulianza Mei 2023 na uligharimu dola milioni 600.
Mabadiliko ya tabia nchi
Takwimu zilizochapishwa mwezi Januari zilifichua kwamba mwaka 2024 ulikuwa mwaka wa kwanza wa kalenda kurekodiwa kuwa na wastani wa halijoto duniani 1.6°C (2.8°F) juu ya viwango vya kabla ya viwanda.
Habari hizo zilikuja karibu muongo mmoja baada ya nchi 195 kupitisha Mkataba wa Hali ya Hewa wa Paris, ambapo walikubaliana kuchukua hatua za kupunguza halijoto duniani ambayo husababisha mabadiliko ya hali ya hewa kutokana na shughuli za binadamu, na kusababisha joto la zaidi 1.5°C, juu ya wastani wa kabla ya viwanda.
Baadaye mwaka huo, mwezi Juni, wanasayansi walitangaza kwamba ongezeko la asidi baharini lilikuwa limezidi kikomo ambacho sayari inaweza kuhimili.
Tiba ya VVU
Njia ya kupata tiba ya VVU ilifichuliwa mwezi Mei wakati watafiti huko Melbourne, Australia, walipotangaza kuwa wamepata njia ya kulazimisha virusi kuondoka kwenye seli za binadamu.
Kabla ya ugunduzi wao, moja ya changamoto kuu katika kutibu VVU ni kwamba virusi vnaweza kujificha kwenye seli nyeupe za damu, ikimaanisha kuwa vinaweza kufufuka wakati wowote.
Watafiti walitumia teknolojia ya mRNA ili kufanya virusi vionekane - mafanikio ambayo hapo awali yalidhaniwa hayawezekani.
Karibu watu milioni 40 duniani kote wanaishi na VVU na hulazimika kutumia dawa za kukandamiza virusi hivyo ili vikosi nguvu.
Watafiti pia wanaamini ugunduzi wao unaweza kusaidia kutibu magonjwa mengine yanayohusisha seli nyeupe za damu, ikiwa ni pamoja na saratani.
Ishara ya maisha katika sayari ya Mirihi
Utafiti kwenye mwamba katika sayari ya Mirihi ulionyesha alama ambazo zinaashiria uwezekano wa kuwepo kwa uhai," kaimu msimamizi wa NASA, Sean Duffy alitangaza mwezi Septemba.
Mwamba huo, unaodhaniwa kuwa na umri wa takriban miaka bilioni 3.5, uligunduliwa na chombo cha NASA cha Perseverance wakati wa uchunguzi wake Julai 2024.
Tangu wakati huo, wanasayansi wa sayari wamekuwa wakijaribu kujua ni nini kiliunda alama hizo. Nadharia kuu ni kwamba zilitoka kwa vijidudu vya kale vya Mirihi.
Ikiwa kila kitu kitaenda kama kilivyopangwa, sampuli ya mwamba huo italetwa Duniani siku moja na kuchunguzwa kwa kina juu ya dalili za maisha ya zamani.
Kutawanyika kwa neutrino kumeonekana
Mwezi Julai, athari inayohusisha neutrino hatimaye ilionekana baada ya miaka 50 ya utafutaji. Kwa mara ya kwanza nadharia hiyo ilielezwa mwaka 1974, ambapo neutrino hutawanyika katika mtambo wa nyuklia dhidi ya kiini cha atomiki.
Wanasayansi wanasema ugunduzi huu ni muhimu na unaweza kuashiria enzi mpya juu ya ugunduzi wa neutrino.
Picha ya kwanza ya kiinitete cha binadamu
Septemba kwa mara ya kwanza kabisa, kiinitete cha binadamu kinapojipandikiza kwenye uterasi bandia kilinaswa kwenye kamera. Video na picha zisizo na mawimbi.
Kushindwa kwa vipandikizi husababisha asilimia 60 ya mimba kuharibika. Watafiti walionasa picha hizo wanatumai watachangia katika uelewa bora wa mchakato huo, ambao unaweza kusaidia kuboresha ya uzazi, katika mimba ya asili na utungisho wa ndani ya kizazi (IVF).
Ulimwengu unapungua kasi
Data iliyotolewa mwezi Machi ilikubaliana na nadharia zilizoanzishwa hapo awali kwamba Ulimwengu unapanuka, lakini iliendelea kupendekeza kwamba kiwango cha kasi kinapungua polepole.
Miezi michache baadaye, mwezi Juni, wanachama wa Mradi wa Kosmolojia ya Supernova walichapisha matokeo mapya ambayo yalionekana kuunga mkono nadhari iliyotolewa mwezi Machi.

title: California Legislature passes balcony solar bill
content:
Next Upcoming
Rural America & The Clean Energy Transition at Climate Week NYC
By Canary Media
Californians could soon put solar panel kits on balconies and in backyards to lower their electric bills — without utility approval.
On Wednesday, state lawmakers passed the Plug and Play Solar Act (Senate Bill 868) to legalize balcony solar, a form of DIY clean energy that’s taken off in Germany. The bill, which garnered bipartisan support, now heads to the desk of Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom. His office declined to say if he’ll sign or veto it within the 30-day deadline; if he does neither, it would still become law and take effect Jan. 1, 2027.
“Imagine being able to reduce your annual electric bill by $400, which is what is estimated here, simply by plugging in one of these devices and leaving it in the sun,” state Sen. Scott Wiener (D), who wrote the bill, said at a Monday press conference on the legislation. “This is a level of convenience in terms of installation and energy savings that we have not seen before.”
Balcony solar kits, already sold by a few businesses in the U.S., put home solar in the hands of millions of renters and homeowners who can’t have panels installed on their roofs. The portable panels push power into a standard 120-volt wall outlet; that electricity then flows to the nearest power-hungry devices, such as the fridge, computer, Wi-Fi router, lights, and air conditioner.
If enacted, California’s legislation would allow households to install plug-in solar systems sized up to 1,200 watts per residence without the costly and potentially time-consuming utility interconnection process that’s required for larger rooftop arrays. Even a 400-watt system can cover roughly 14% of an apartment’s energy use, according to the Environmental Working Group, a nonprofit that advocated for the bill.
The Golden State’s embrace of balcony solar follows a tsunami of support nationwide. More than half of states have considered plug-in solar legislation in the last year, and so far, eight have adopted balcony solar laws: Colorado, Connecticut, Maine, Maryland, New Hampshire, Utah, Vermont, and Virginia. New York passed a bill in June, but boosters are still on tenterhooks as to whether Gov. Kathy Hochul (D) will sign it.
“California is going to have a huge impact on this market,” said Cora Stryker, co-founder of plug-in solar nonprofit Bright Saver. The state’s economy is the largest and among the fastest growing in the nation. “Manufacturers are going to see this and seize upon the opportunity.”
The bad news: Households won’t be able to get plug-in solar that meets the bill’s requirements right away. The state would allow only balcony solar kits that have been certified safe to use by a nationally recognized testing laboratory. One of these organizations, safety company UL Solutions, began testing plug-in systems this year under its new standard, UL 3700, but no product has yet earned certification.
The rule is more restrictive than those adopted by some other states. For example, Utah and Maryland require that the individual kit components pass safety standards, rather than the entire system, according to Stryker.
Stryker said she’s worried that California’s stringent approach could put a damper on balcony solar’s growth in the state in the near term, especially for renters. In its current form, the UL 3700 standard still requires an electrician to get involved, the opposite of plug and play. Still, Bernadette Del Chiaro, the Environmental Working Group’s senior vice president for California, said she expects the standard to evolve to include DIY systems as soon as next year.
Another wrinkle: The legislation includes an expiration date, which the state’s largest utility, Pacific Gas and Electric, appears to have lobbied for. On Jan. 1, 2030, Californians will no longer be able to install plug-in solar without first getting their utility’s sign off.
“We would expect the Legislature to reconsider that sunset in 2028 and at the latest 2029,” Del Chiaro said.
Wiener believes, despite its challenges, the plug-in solar bill will be transformative for Californians. “Balcony solar is incredibly important,” Wiener told Canary Media. “This is a way to lower people’s cost of living when people need relief. … I’m glad that we’re finally making it happen.”

title: Israel to return remains of Palestinian child held for more than 9 months
content:
Israel has decided to hand over the body of a 15-year-old Palestinian boy more than nine months after Israeli forces killed him and withheld his remains, a Palestinian group said on Wednesday.
The National Campaign for the Retrieval of Palestinian Martyrs’ Bodies said Jadallah Jihad Jumaa Jadallah from the Al-Fara’a refugee camp in Tubas was killed by Israeli army fire during a raid on the camp on November 16 2025.
His body has remained in Israeli custody since then.
The campaign said the decision followed a petition filed with the Israeli Supreme Court in March demanding the return of the child’s body.
After repeatedly granting prosecutors more time to respond, the court received notice on Wednesday that Israeli authorities intended to hand over the body in the coming days, though no specific date was given.
The campaign said withholding Jadallah’s body for more than nine months had deprived his family of the right to bid him farewell and bury him.
In figures released on Wednesday ahead of the annual National Day for the Retrieval of Palestinian Martyrs’ Bodies, the group said Israel is holding the remains of around 1,700 Palestinians, including 799 whose identities are known.
Among the identified bodies are those of 81 children, 99 Palestinians who died in Israeli prisons and 10 women, it said.
The campaign said another 256 bodies are held in so-called “cemeteries of numbers,” where graves are marked with numbers rather than names and Israel retains information on the identities of those buried there.
Israel’s Supreme Court ruled in 2019 that authorities could withhold Palestinian bodies for use as bargaining chips, a policy that was later expanded to cover Palestinians accused by Israel of carrying out attacks.

title: Κίνα: Θεραπεία με βλαστοκύτταρα ανέστρεψε την καρδιακή ανεπάρκεια στο 90% των ασθενών σε κλινική δοκιμή
content:
12:44 23/08
Εντόπισαν πρώιμα σημάδια για καρκίνο του μαστού ως και έξι χρόνια πριν από τη διάγνωση με τη βοήθεια τεχνητής νοημοσύνης
Η μελέτη, στην οποία συμμετέχουν και Ελληνες επιστήμονες, ανοίγει τον δρόμο για πιο έγκαιρη ανίχνευση της νόσου.
Μια πρωτοποριακή θεραπεία με βλαστοκύτταρα ανέστρεψε τη σοβαρή καρδιακή ανεπάρκεια στο 90% των ασθενών, σύμφωνα με κλινική δοκιμή που διεξήχθη στην Κίνα.
Οι ασθενείς με καρδιακή ανεπάρκεια εμφανίζουν συμπτώματα όπως δύσπνοια, κόπωση, πρήξιμο στα πόδια, απότομη αύξηση του σωματικού βάρους και επίμονο βήχα. Αν και η μεταμόσχευση καρδιάς αποτελεί σήμερα την κύρια θεραπευτική επιλογή για την αντιμετώπιση της πάθησης, οι διαθέσιμοι δότες είναι περιορισμένοι.
Τώρα, ερευνητές από το Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital στην Κίνα έδειξαν ότι η θεραπεία με βλαστοκύτταρα μπορεί να οδηγήσει στην ανάπτυξη νέου καρδιακού ιστού και να αποκαταστήσει τη λειτουργία της καρδιάς σε 9 στους 10 ασθενείς με καρδιακή ανεπάρκεια, ενώ παράλληλα μπορεί να συμβάλει στην επιβράδυνση της γήρανσης του καρδιακού μυός.
Στην κλινική δοκιμή, 10 ασθενείς υποβλήθηκαν σε έγχυση βλαστοκυττάρων, τα οποία μπορούν να αναπτυχθούν και να διαφοροποιηθούν σε εξειδικευμένα κύτταρα του καρδιακού μυός. Αρχικά, τα ίδια κύτταρα μετατράπηκαν σε επαγόμενα πολυδύναμα βλαστοκύτταρα (iPSCs). Στη συνέχεια, αυτά διαφοροποιήθηκαν σε κύτταρα του καρδιακού μυός και εγχύθηκαν στις κατεστραμμένες περιοχές της καρδιάς. Στην ομάδα ελέγχου συμμετείχαν 10 επιπλέον ασθενείς, οι οποίοι υποβλήθηκαν σε επέμβαση αορτοστεφανιαίας παράκαμψης (bypass).
Οι ερευνητές παρακολούθησαν την καρδιακή λειτουργία των ασθενών μέσω απεικονιστικών εξετάσεων, εργαστηριακών ελέγχων και αξιολογήσεων. Διαπιστώθηκε ότι οι 9 από τους 10 ασθενείς που έλαβαν τα βλαστοκύτταρα παρουσίασαν σημαντική βελτίωση της καρδιακής λειτουργίας κατά την παρακολούθηση διάρκειας 12 μηνών.
Η καρδιακή τους λειτουργία βελτιώθηκε σημαντικά, επιτρέποντάς τους να ανταποκρίνονται στις καθημερινές δραστηριότητες. Παράλληλα, οι ερευνητές κατέγραψαν σημαντική υποχώρηση της πίεσης στο στήθος και της δύσπνοιας.
Οι ασθενείς παρουσίασαν επίσης καλύτερες επιδόσεις στο τεστ βάδισης έξι λεπτών, όπου η επίδοσή τους βελτιώθηκε σχεδόν δύο φορές περισσότερο σε σύγκριση με την ομάδα ελέγχου.
Οι επιστήμονες διαπίστωσαν επίσης ότι, κατά μέσο όρο, οι καρδιές των ασθενών παρουσίασαν βελτίωση στην ποσότητα αίματος που εξωθείται σε κάθε καρδιακό παλμό μετά τη θεραπεία με βλαστοκύτταρα. Αντίθετα, μόνο το 60% των ασθενών της ομάδας ελέγχου παρουσίασε αντίστοιχο επίπεδο βελτίωσης, ενώ ένας ασθενής πέθανε οκτώ μήνες μετά την επέμβαση.
Σύμφωνα με τους ερευνητές, δεν καταγράφηκαν σοβαρές ανεπιθύμητες ενέργειες στους ασθενείς που έλαβαν τη θεραπεία.
"Κλινικά σημαντική ταχυκαρδία, η οποία εμφανίστηκε σε δύο ασθενείς, κορυφώθηκε δύο έως τρεις εβδομάδες μετά τη διαδικασία και υποχώρησε πλήρως", σημείωσαν οι ερευνητές.
Ωστόσο, οι επιστήμονες υπογραμμίζουν ότι απαιτούνται περαιτέρω μελέτες προκειμένου να προσδιοριστεί με μεγαλύτερη ακρίβεια η σχέση "οφέλους-κινδύνου" της θεραπείας με iPSCs.

title: ‘They make life much easier’: AI-powered shopping trolleys go on trial in Lancashire
content:
Lancashire has been the site of many British innovations throughout history, from the spinning jenny, which transformed textile production, to the creation of jelly babies.
Now it has welcomed another first: AI shopping trolleys.
A Morrisons in Lancashire has become the first supermarket in the UK to trial the use of “smart trolleys” that allow customers to do their shopping without having to scan a single item.
The AI-powered Caper smart trolleys, created by San Francisco-based Instacart, automatically register each item placed in the trolley, adding up the cost and recommending related products as you shop. Once finished, customers can scan their trolley screen rather than visiting a checkout.
Preston is the first city in Britain to use them after the supermarket chain announced a deal to trial them at its location in Ashton-on-Ribble, to the west of the city.
Amazon Fresh, which allowed shoppers to take items from the shelves and leave the shop without checking out, using cameras to charge directly to online accounts, failed to take off in the UK, with the company’s last physical British store closing in 2025. But Morrisons is more hopeful that its smart trolleys will be a success, with plans to put them in supermarkets across the country.
The smart trolleys are already used in more than 100 cities across the world. They are similar in design and function to the Dash Cart used by Amazon’s Fresh stores, which still operate outside the UK.
After the trolleys rolled into Ashton-on-Ribble last month, customer Matthew Byrne said they had “massively” helped him keep track of his shopping. Byrne is autistic and struggles to stick to set plans for what to get from the shops.
“Having what I’ve bought on screen has been great. I have a habit of just grabbing things and throwing them in my trolley, and then wondering how I’m paying so much. It’s been amazing to visualise it and see it in real time. I came here with an £80 budget, and I’ve actually been able to stick to it.”
Kaz Bond was disappointed to be forced to use a normal trolley for her latest shop due to a fault on her phone, having used them for every trip she has made to Morrisons since they became commonplace around four weeks ago.
“Honestly, I think they’re brilliant,” said Bond. “They make life much easier. I wouldn’t be that surprised if they’re everywhere before long. I reckon it’s the future.”
Debbie Files had chosen Tuesday as the day to take a leap of faith and use the trolleys for the first time, albeit with the help of a Morrisons employee.
“It was a little bit confusing at first, but you get used to it pretty quickly,” said Files. “It’s heavy, though. I’ve barely been able to turn it. I feel like I need a driving lesson to use it, but I got the hang of it. If they make a smaller one then that will get me to use it again.”

title: Los negocios que activa el boom energético y el cuello de botella que amenaza con frenarlos
content:
Los negocios que activa el boom energético y el cuello de botella que amenaza con frenarlos
Según sus ejecutivos, AKROS proyecta parques por US$265 millones y Grupo L invirtió $2500 millones en su base neuquina; la provincia de Buenos Aires advierte que la falta de transporte eléctrico y contenido local condicionan el crecimiento
- 6 minutos de lectura'
Una papa pelada y cortada puede recorrer 400 kilómetros antes de terminar en un plato de comida servido a 4000 metros de altura. El recorrido parece desproporcionado para un producto tan sencillo, pero permite dimensionar parte de la estructura que se mueve detrás de una mina, un yacimiento o una planta instalada lejos de los centros urbanos.
Grupo L se ocupa de que ese plato llegue a destino. La empresa argentina tiene 7200 colaboradores, está presente en 15 provincias y brinda alimentación, limpieza, hotelería y mantenimiento en sitios remotos, según explicó Marcelo Delbarba, director de Desarrollo de Negocios, Relaciones Institucionales y Comunicación de la compañía.
Al mismo tiempo, en Neuquén, una desarrolladora que comenzó con proyectos inmobiliarios urbanos impulsa dos parques de energías renovables con una potencia conjunta cercana a los 200 MW y una inversión estimada de US$288 millones. AKROS también proyecta una base logística, productiva y residencial sobre un campo de 7685 hectáreas, de acuerdo con su socia gerente, Alicia E. Henríquez.
Entre ambos proyectos aparece el mismo fenómeno, donde el crecimiento de la actividad energética ya derrama negocios sobre otros sectores, pero también expone los límites de la infraestructura y de la capacidad productiva local.
Gastón Ghioni, subsecretario de Energía de la provincia de Buenos Aires, puso el foco en uno de ellos y cómo la falta de transporte eléctrico de alta tensión impide sumar nuevos proyectos y amenaza con dejar a la generación por detrás del avance del petróleo y el gas.
Los tres participaron de uno de los paneles del capítulo 4 de Energía, organizado por LA NACION, y moderado por la periodista Carla Quiroga, donde analizaron las inversiones que buscan anticiparse al crecimiento y los límites que todavía condicionan su expansión.
El negocio de llegar antes
En los sitios remotos, la primera obligación no es crecer. Es no detenerse. “El servicio no puede parar nunca”, resumió Delbarba. Grupo L puede montar una cocina para alimentar a 800 personas a 3000 metros de altura, pero también debe llegar hasta la boca de un pozo donde trabajan cuatro operarios. La escala cambia, pero no la necesidad de continuidad.
Esa exigencia llevó a la compañía a inaugurar en abril una planta elaboradora y un centro logístico en Neuquén. La inversión fue cercana a los $2500 millones, según el ejecutivo, e incluyó un lavadero industrial capaz de procesar hasta 700 prendas y artículos de blanquería por día y una escuela de gastronomía.
La lógica consiste en trasladar tareas hacia la base para reducir residuos y movimientos de personal en el destino. Si un campamento todavía no tiene instalaciones definitivas, utilizan cocinas móviles. “Todo esto termina en un plato de comida caliente a 4000 metros”, explicó. El despliegue también abre la pregunta de dónde se instalarán las personas, los camiones y los servicios que necesitarán esos proyectos a medida que aumente la actividad.
De los proyectos urbanos a Vaca Muerta
AKROS lleva más de dos décadas vinculada con el desarrollo urbano y la construcción en Neuquén, pero hace aproximadamente ocho años, sus socios decidieron diversificarse y adquirieron propiedades rurales de gran extensión. “En nuestra región lo que sobra es tierra, sol y viento”, explicó Henríquez.
Uno de sus proyectos es el parque eólico Las Campanas, previsto en el departamento de Picún Leufú. Contempla 31 aerogeneradores, una potencia de 184,5 MW y una inversión estimada de US$275 millones. Su superficie técnica será de aproximadamente 3500 hectáreas dentro de una propiedad de 7697 hectáreas.
El segundo es el parque solar Patagonia Norte I, de 15 MW de potencia nominal y 18,3 MWp, proyectado sobre 38,3 hectáreas. La inversión estimada asciende a US$13 millones. En conjunto, ambas iniciativas suman 199,5 MW y demandarían US$288 millones.
Según la empresa, los dos proyectos completaron la evaluación de impacto ambiental, la licencia correspondiente y las gestiones ante CAMMESA. Actualmente avanzan en la ingeniería de detalle, la selección final de tecnología y el cierre financiero. “Todo depende de lo que uno pueda insertar en la red”, reconoció Henríquez.
Dentro del predio de 7685 hectáreas donde se emplazará el parque solar, AKROS también desarrolla Rincón Buena Esperanza Hub, que abarca 351 hectáreas sobre la Ruta Provincial 17, entre Añelo y Cutral Co–Plaza Huincul, e incluye áreas logísticas, productivas, residenciales y de servicios. La primera etapa prevé 110 espacios para camiones de gran porte, con capacidad para llegar a 250.
El límite de la red
El limitante de infraestructura conecta las inversiones privadas con el diagnóstico de Ghioni. Según el funcionario, la provincia de Buenos Aires concentra cerca del 40% de la generación eléctrica nacional y una proporción similar de la eólica. Pero, sin más transporte, advirtió, no podrán incorporarse nuevos parques. Mientras la producción de petróleo y gas avanzó acompañada por nuevos ductos y proyectos de exportación, sostuvo, el sistema eléctrico quedó rezagado.
Para Ghioni, la transición energética también exige definir qué componentes, tecnología y empleo puede aportar la Argentina. Mencionó licitaciones eólicas en las que, según indicó, llegaron a importarse todos los elementos de las torres. “La transición energética tiene que hacerse con los argentinos adentro”, afirmó.
El funcionario vinculó esa discusión con el Régimen de Incentivo para Grandes Inversiones (RIGI), al que cuestionó por no exigir suficiente contenido nacional. “No solamente no incentiva, sino que desincentiva la producción local”, sostuvo.
Sin embargo, Henríquez, desde la mirada empresaria, apuntó que la apertura económica, la estabilidad cambiaria y la seguridad jurídica pueden acelerar los proyectos. En ese contexto, planteó que importar aerogeneradores de fabricantes especializados permite reducir la curva de aprendizaje y acortar los plazos. “Podemos tenerlos en un plazo muy corto, lo que contribuye a la rentabilidad de la inversión y del negocio”, explicó.
Delbarba llevó la tensión al terreno operativo. Advirtió que muchos proveedores locales todavía no alcanzan la escala requerida y que una operación puede necesitar módulos para 800 personas y servicios diarios para hasta 5000 trabajadores. “El negocio no frena para esperar”, sintetizó.
Para Ghioni, allí aparece el papel del Estado. Como ejemplo, mencionó una subestación construida con una cooperativa en una localidad bonaerense de 900 habitantes. La inversión fue de $4000 millones y multiplicó por diez la capacidad disponible, según relató. Dos meses después de su inauguración ya había recibido tres solicitudes de conexión para proyectos productivos.

title: Registro Único de Vivienda abre a nivel nacional: ¿qué se necesita y dónde acudir?
content:
Registro Único de Vivienda abre a nivel nacional: ¿qué se necesita y dónde acudir?
Para el Registro Único de Vivienda se requiere la cédula de identidad laminada, información del núcleo familiar y la ubicación exacta del inmueble afectado. Al finalizar, el sistema generará un código QR que respaldará la asignación de la vivienda
El Ministerio del Poder Popular para Hábitat y Vivienda (Minhvi) habilitó este miércoles 19 de agosto el Registro Único de Vivienda a nivel nacional. Según las autoridades, esta plataforma permitirá identificar a las familias afectadas por el doblete sísmico del 24 de junio para gestionar la asignación de soluciones habitacionales.
El proceso comenzó en La Guaira, en los refugios temporales habilitados después de la emergencia. Ahora el registro se puede hacer desde las oficinas estadales del Minhvi, en un horario de 8:00 a.m. a 12:00 p.m. Quienes estén en Caracas también pueden acudir al Banco Nacional de Vivienda y Hábitat (Banavih) para censarse.
Para el Registro Único de Vivienda se requiere la cédula de identidad laminada, información del núcleo familiar y la ubicación exacta del inmueble afectado. Al finalizar, el sistema generará un código QR que respaldará la asignación de la vivienda
Si la persona perdió sus documentos durante los sismos, la plataforma realiza una validación biométrica mediante un captahuellas. Este dispositivo consulta directamente la base de datos del Servicio Administrativo de Identificación, Migración y Extranjería (Saime) para corroborar su identidad.
En entrevista con Unión Radio, la ministra de Hábitat y Vivienda, Paola Posani, detalló que unas 40.000 familias ya fueron registradas, lo que se traduce en aproximadamente 128.000 personas. Del total, 32.000 corresponden a La Guaira. Igualmente, la arquitecto informó que el registro incluye familias de La Guaira, Caracas, Miranda, Aragua, Falcón, Carabobo y Yaracuy que se vieron afectadas por el doblete sísmico.
La ministra Posani señaló que la meta en lo que resta del año es construir unas 4.000 viviendas en todo el país. Para ello, se están reactivando obras en Mérida, Monagas, Aragua, Carabobo, Caracas, La Guaira, Zulia, Amazonas, Trujillo y Nueva Esparta. «Estamos revisando las obras que quedaron en estructura con buen acabado; las estamos retomando para tener un número importante este año», acotó.

Este contenido fue escrito tomando en consideración las amenazas y límites que, en consecuencia, se han impuesto a la divulgación de informaciones desde dentro del país.

title: Schutzangebot: Schutzwohnung für Männer als Opfer von Gewalt in der Familie
content:
Für Männer, die von häuslicher Gewalt betroffen sind, gibt es in Darmstadt nun eine eigene Schutzwohnung. Das Angebot ist Teil eines Pilotprojekts in Hessen und soll Betroffenen einen sicheren Rückzugsort bieten. Nach dem jüngsten Lagebild «Häusliche Gewalt» des Bundeskriminalamtes (BKA) für 2024 sind knapp 30 Prozent der erfassten Opfer Männer. Demnach ist der überwiegende Teil der Opfer von Gewalt durch den Partner oder in der Familie Frauen.
In der Wohnung in Darmstadt gibt es nach Aussagen von Boris von Heesen vom Verein Flexible Jugendhilfe, der das Pilotprojekt betreut, zwei Einzelzimmer für Männer sowie ein Zimmer für zwei Kinder. «Laut Konzept werden bis zu zwei Männer in der Wohnung sozialpädagogisch begleitet, um sich zu stabilisieren, Ruhe zu finden und Kraft für einen Neustart zu sammeln.»

title: La Ville de Paris annonce la « mise à l’abri » de 250 personnes, migrantes pour la plupart, qui étaient installées sur le parvis de la mairie de Paris Centre
content:
La Ville de Paris a annoncé, samedi 22 août, « la mise à l’abri de l’ensemble des 253 personnes », des migrants essentiellement, « installées devant la mairie de Paris Centre », à la suite de l’« évacuation forcée » par l’Etat du campement établi en juillet dans l’enceinte du Samusocial, à l’occasion d’une grève d’agents de l’organisme.
Le campement, situé à proximité du quartier touristique du Marais, abritait quelque 400 personnes, dont des étrangers en situation régulière et des sans-papiers, pour certains évacués il y a plus d’une semaine du camp de fortune du Samusocial, dans le 13e arrondissement. Une situation dénoncée par les associations, qui fustigent régulièrement le manque d’hébergement d’urgence dans la capitale.
« La Ville de Paris annonce aujourd’hui l’engagement de la mise à l’abri de l’ensemble des personnes présentes sur ce site », affirme samedi la Mairie dans un communiqué. « L’ensemble des personnes installées sur le parvis de la mairie de Paris Centre sont désormais mises à l’abri au sein de gymnases de la Ville », ajoute la Mairie, « jusqu’à ce que les services de l’Etat, dont c’est la responsabilité légale et morale, leur proposent une solution pérenne ».
« C’est un véritable soulagement pour ces familles dont l’état de santé ne cessait de se dégrader », a déclaré à l’Agence France-Presse Méryl Sotty, porte-parole de Médecins sans frontières, dont les équipes ont effectué sept interventions depuis la mi-juillet sur le campement du Samusocial puis devant la mairie de Paris.
Selon Luc Viger, coordinateur pour l’Ile-de-France de l’association Utopia56, « 50 personnes restent sans solution » et vont se « retrouver dès ce soir à la permanence quotidienne de l’association », qui sollicite son réseau pour trouver des places d’hébergement chez des bénévoles.
« Je ne peux pas accepter que Paris se substitue indéfiniment à l’Etat »
Mi-août, le campement du Samusocial, qui avait rassemblé jusqu’à 450 sans-abri, a été évacué par les forces de l’ordre. « Toutes les personnes présentes sur le site du Samusocial ce matin ont reçu une proposition d’hébergement », avait alors assuré la Préfecture de police (PP) de Paris, mais « certains occupants n’ont pas souhaité bénéficier des solutions proposées et se retrouvent désormais à la rue, en pleine canicule ».
La PP et la préfecture de région avaient justifié leur décision en raison de la proximité du campement avec la route et d’un trafic « particulièrement dense ». Les autorités mettaient aussi en avant des « conditions d’hygiène » devenues « particulièrement préoccupantes » avec un « accès totalement insuffisant à l’eau et aux toilettes ».
« Je refuse que des familles et des enfants soient remis à la rue sans solution et j’ai donc pris mes responsabilités en mobilisant les moyens de la Ville pour mettre à l’abri ce matin 253 personnes », déclare le maire de la capitale, Emmanuel Grégoire, cité dans le communiqué. « Je ne peux pas accepter que Paris se substitue indéfiniment à l’Etat, alors même que l’hébergement d’urgence relève de sa responsabilité et que 300 places ont été récemment supprimées », prévient en outre l’élu socialiste.

title: Conheça os novos trainees da Pública
content:
Em agosto de 2026, a Agência Pública lançou seu primeiro programa de trainee. O Curso Pública de Jornalismo é um programa de treinamento intensivo, prático e imersivo, com duração de seis meses, voltado para dez jornalistas recém-formados, que inclui aulas online, mentorias profissionais, elaboração de um projeto aprofundado e um período de prática presencial na redação da Pública em São Paulo ou Brasília. O treinamento é voltado exclusivamente para pessoas autodeclaradas negras, indígenas e trans que tenham concluído a graduação de jornalismo nos últimos três anos.
O Curso Pública de Jornalismo é mais uma iniciativa da Pública de fomento ao jornalismo independente, em parceria com a Fundação Itaú e a Imaginable Futures.
Conheça abaixo os dez jornalistas selecionados para o Curso Pública de Jornalismo 2026.
Aldrey Olegario
Jornalista formada pela Universidade de São Paulo. Nascida em Piracicaba (SP), já passou pela redação da revista Marie Claire Brasil, onde escreveu para as redes sociais e para a editoria de cultura, e pelo Instituto de Química da USP. Tem interesse em jornalismo científico e em reportagens aprofundadas e explicativas. No seu Trabalho de Conclusão de Curso, pesquisou a exposição ao amianto em Osasco (SP), em livro-reportagem premiado no Intercom Sudeste.
Ariel Giagio
Nascido em São Paulo, é graduado em Jornalismo pela Cásper Líbero e faz mestrado em Humanidades, Direitos Humanos e outras Legitimidades na USP, onde pesquisa a intersecção entre audiovisual, filantropia e deficiência. Trabalhou na produtora Deus Dará, com redação de projetos para editais de fomento cultural e com produção audiovisual. Participou também da produção da 4° temporada da série Idade Mídia, do canal Futura. Tem experiência em assessoria de imprensa e coordenação de redes sociais. Como homem trans, procura amplificar as vozes que vieram antes dele e que o ajudaram a cultivar sua autoconfiança. Acredita no poder da linguagem de transformar vidas, desde que usada de forma genuína e responsável. Buscando esse objetivo, se capacitou em cinco línguas além do português, incluindo Língua Brasileira de Sinais.
Cecília Melo
Jornalista e pesquisadora. Filha de Arlete Oliveira, professora de português, e de Dario Dias, pescador e aquaviário, é nascida e criada na região da Reserva de Desenvolvimento Sustentável Estadual Ponta do Tubarão, em Diogo Lopes, no Rio Grande do Norte. Cursa o mestrado em Estudos da Mídia na Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte, onde também graduou-se em Jornalismo. Foi estagiária do Jornal Agora RN, da Revista Cultue e do Canal Consulta Pública. Também foi estagiária de jornalismo do Instituto Federal do Rio Grande do Norte. É idealizadora e produtora do jornal comunitário “Vozes da Reserva”, que cobre a vida dos moradores de Ponta do Tubarão.
Grazy Kaimbé
É jornalista, formada pela Universidade Federal da Bahia (UFBA). Nascida e criada na Terra Indígena Massacará, no interior da Bahia, hoje é moradora de Salvador. Foi estagiária da TV Bahia, onde também participou do grupo de pesquisa, montagem e edição do documentário Ilê Aiyê: A Casa do Mundo. Fez parte da 9ª turma do Treinamento em Jornalismo em Ciência e Saúde da Folha de S.Paulo. Foi repórter do caderno 2+, da edição impressa do jornal A Tarde, onde também cobriu a editoria de Salvador nos fins de semana. Dirigiu e editou o documentário sobre os 20 anos da Articulação dos Povos Indígenas do Brasil (Apib). É membro da Articulação Brasileira de Indígenas Jornalistas (Abrinjor). Fez a cobertura da COP30 pela Mídia Indígena, maior coletivo de comunicação indígena do Brasil, onde atualmente atua como repórter.
Igor de Paula
Jornalista formado pela Universidade Federal do Espírito Santo (UFES). Capixaba da gema, possui mais de três anos de experiência prática em comunicação de instituições públicas de destaque, como Ministério Público do Estado do Espírito Santo e a Secretaria da Ciência, Tecnologia, Inovação e Educação Profissional do Estado do Espírito Santo. Tem interesse por impactos da tecnologia e desinformação na sociedade, bem como pautas socioambientais e direitos humanos utilizando dados públicos. Pesquisa novas formas de aplicação do jornalismo de dados no jornalismo local.
Lucas Bezerra
Comunicólogo pela Universidade Federal de Pernambuco. Nascido em Garanhuns e criado em Jupi, no Agreste pernambucano. Tem passagem pelos veículos #Colabora e O Joio e o Trigo, onde atuou na produção de reportagens sobre direitos humanos, meio ambiente e alimentação. Também tem experiência com pesquisa para podcast, gerenciamento de redes sociais, bem como com gestão de audiência e de comunidades. Foi ainda estagiário de comunicação do Centro Cultural Brasil Alemanha.
Lucas Henrique Santos
Nascido e criado na periferia da zona sul de São Paulo, é jornalista formado pela Universidade Presbiteriana Mackenzie. Foi estagiário da Record News por quase três anos, passando pelas áreas de redes sociais, assessoria de imprensa e de edição de textos. Em sua trajetória acadêmica, pesquisou desertos de notícias e fez uma análise comparativa entre a cobertura de segurança pública na periferia, a partir das lentes do jornal O Estado de S. Paulo e da Ponte Jornalismo. É movido pelo propósito de dar visibilidade a realidades e territórios frequentemente marginalizados pela mídia tradicional.
Muximba
É jornalista pela Universidade Federal do Amapá (UNIFAP) e reside em Macapá – AP. Atua em comunicação popular, jornalismo independente, comunicação científica e produção audiovisual, com foco em direitos humanos, justiça climática, raça e territórios amazônicos. Integra a equipe do Instituto Mapinguari, onde desenvolve estratégias de comunicação e projetos voltados à incidência política em pautas de clima e meio ambiente. Dirigiu três documentários exibidos em festivais e mostras regionais e nacionais. É uma pessoa negra e não-binária, nascida e criada na Amazônia e acredita na comunicação como ferramenta para fortalecer narrativas produzidas a partir dos territórios.
Nathália Baron
Formada em Artes Cênicas pela Escola Técnica Estadual de Artes e em Jornalismo na Faculdades Metropolitanas Unidas. Durante a graduação, foi três vezes vencedora do Prêmio Valoriza de Jornalismo e Relações Públicas da FMU. Um dos prêmios foi para a reportagem de dados “Úteros em cárcere: grávidas e crianças sob a negligência do sistema prisional brasileiro”. Seu Trabalho de Conclusão de Curso, o livro-reportagem “Egressas: as sobreviventes do sistema prisional”, reúne relatos de mulheres que reconstruíram suas vidas após o cárcere. Foi estagiária e assistente nas agências de assessoria e de marketing APIS3, Ecomunica e Monks, bem como analista no Reclame Aqui. Nascida e criada em São Paulo, Nathália busca dar visibilidade a pessoas e realidades frequentemente rotuladas como “marginais”. Tem interesse em cobrir segurança pública e direitos humanos.
Nicole Santos
Jornalista formada pela Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul, já atuou com reportagem, produção de conteúdo digital e comunicação para diferentes plataformas. Nasceu e cresceu em Porto Alegre, mas hoje é moradora de São Paulo. Foi estagiária de redes sociais e da editoria de economia no jornal Correio do Povo. Durante esse período, foi finalista do Prêmio Sebrae de Jornalismo e descobriu sua paixão pela economia. Foi também redatora e social media na Agência WT.AG. Sua pesquisa acadêmica focou na ausência de mulheres negras nas redações dos principais jornais do Rio Grande do Sul, buscando compreender a influência das desigualdades estruturais nas narrativas jornalísticas. Além da economia, tem interesse em investigar temas relacionados a gênero, raça e direitos humanos.

title: Ny medisin mot dødelig bukspyttkjertelkreft godkjent i USA
content:
Ny medisin mot dødelig bukspyttkjertelkreft godkjent i USA
En ny medisin for å behandle en av de dødeligste kreftformene som finnes, er godkjent for bruk i USA.
Medisinen, som har merkenavnet Rasonque, er utviklet av den amerikanske oppstartbedriften Revolution Medicines. En klinisk studie viste at den kunne doble hvor lenge enkelte pasienter hadde igjen å leve.
– Dagens godkjenning tilbyr et viktig nytt alternativ for pasienter som står overfor en kreftform som er ekstraordinært krevende og notorisk vanskelig å behandle, sier fungerende kommissær Kyle Diamantas i Food and Drug Administration (FDA) i USA.
Pillen kan ikke kurere bukspyttkjertelkreft, men behandlingen har skapt optimisme hos både onkologer og pasientenes interessegrupper. Potensielt kan enkelte få forlenget livet med flere måneder.
Pillen skal tas daglig. En måneds forbruk vil koste opp mot 39.800 dollar, ifølge selskapet.
Behandlingen bruker et molekyl kalt daraxonrasib og har vist seg langt mer effektivt enn standard cellegift i de kliniske studiene som er utført.
Halvparten av pasientene som fikk pillen overlevde i over 13 måneder, dobbelt så lenge som pasientene som fikk cellegift.
Resultatene har fått stor anerkjennelse i medisinsamfunnet og omtales som det første store gjennombruddet i kampen mot bukspyttkjertelkreft på tiår.

title: Frauen zahlen, Männer nicht: Betroffene wollen sich WC-Klage gegen die Stadt Wien anschließen [premium]
content:
Es war der Sommer nach dem ersten Corona-Jahr. Schön langsam bekamen alle eine Impfung (die eine wollten), man konnte wieder hinaus und sich relativ sorglos treffen. Das tat auch Melanie Gradik. Die damals 22-Jährige zog es wie viele andere junge Leute in den Wiener Stadtpark, „und dort fiel es mir zum ersten Mal auf“: Bei den öffentlichen Toiletten musste sie ins Geldbörsel greifen, ihr männlicher Freund nicht.
Nur 50 Cent, könnte man jetzt sagen, so viel kosten viele der versperrbaren öffentlichen Toiletten in Wien, während Pissoirs gratis zugänglich sind. Aber es summiert sich: „Das ist immer wieder passiert, ich muss ja fast jede Stunde pinkeln.“ Doch Gradik geht es vor allem ums Prinzip: Warum muss sie, nur weil sie eine Frau ist, mehr zahlen? Deswegen klagt sie die Stadt Wien wegen Diskriminierung.
»Alleine sind es 50 Cent. Gemeinsam ist es ein Präzedenzfall.«
Petra LabackRechtsanwältin
Sammelklage geplant
Am Donnerstag hat die Anwältin Petra Laback, die Gradik pro bono vertritt, bekannt gegeben, dass eine Sammelklage angestrebt wird, und sich nun auch andere Frauen dem Anliegen anschließen können: „Alleine sind es 50 Cent. Gemeinsam ist es ein Präzedenzfall.“ Labacks Rechtsmeinung: Die Tatsache, dass es für Frauen keine kostenlose Alternative wie die Pissoirs gibt, verstoße gegen das Wiener Antidiskriminierungsgesetz.
»Wir können uns nicht so schnell erleichtern. Wenn ich nicht 50 Cent mithabe und in den Busch muss, sitzen da wieder Typen mit ihren Handys und machen Fotos. Das ist nicht gerecht.«
Melanie Gradik
Tatsächlich sind von 167 öffentlichen WC-Anlagen, die von der MA 48 betreut werden, 138 kostenlos. In 27 Anlagen kostet die Nutzung der Kabine während der Betreuungszeiten 50 Cent. Die Nutzung des Pissoirs daneben im Männerbereich ist gratis. Auch, um das öffentliche Urinieren hintanzuhalten. „Es sind aber oft genau die Toiletten, die an den Hotspots stehen, im Stadtpark, im Prater, auf der Donauinsel. Da sind viele Menschen, und viele Frauen. Wir können uns nicht so schnell erleichtern. Wenn ich nicht 50 Cent mithabe und in den Busch muss, sitzen da wieder Typen mit ihren Handys und machen Fotos.“ Ihr selbst sei das noch nicht passiert, aber einigen Freundinnen. „Das ist nicht gerecht.“
Gradik führt den Kampf schon länger. Eigentlich seit diesem Abend im Stadtpark. Kurz darauf schrieb sie das erste Mal an die Stadt Wien, bekam eine ernüchternde Antwort, dann nichts mehr. Die Antidiskriminierungsstelle der Stadt Wien, die sie 2024 einschaltete, war aufgeschlossener. Deren Versuche, verwaltungsintern eine Änderung herbeizuführen, liefen jedoch ins Leere.
Stadt Wien: „Unterschiede in der Blasenentleerung“
Das geht aus einem Mail hervor, das Gradik zwei Jahre später bekam, und das der „Presse am Sonntag“ vorliegt: „Wir haben die zuständigen Stellen auf unsere Rechtsansicht, wonach eine unterschiedliche Bezahlung von Pissoir und Kabinentoiletten eine Diskriminierung aufgrund des Geschlechts darstellen würde, mehrfach hingewiesen und uns sehr lange bemüht, ein Einlenken zu erwirken.“ Die Stadt Wien vertrete jedoch die Meinung, dass „die unterschiedliche Behandlung auf physische Unterschiede in der Art der Miktion“ (Begriff für Blasenentleerung, Anm.) zurückzuführen sei. Der „Tatbestand der Diskriminierung“ sei deswegen nicht erfüllt.
Viele Frauen, viele Versuche
Die Stadt stützte sich dabei auf eine Entscheidung der Gleichbehandlungskommission des Bundes, die 2010 ein ähnliches Anliegen einer Bürgerin abwies. Gradik ist also nicht die Erste, der diese Schieflage auffällt. Mehrere Petitionen wurden eingebracht, 2025 kritisierte die Volksanwältin Gaby Schwarz den Umstand. „Mir schreiben so viele Frauen, die es auch bereits bei der Stadt versucht haben“, sagt Gradik. 71 Frauen haben innerhalb von zwei Tagen auf der Homepage 50cent.at Interesse an der Sammelklage angemeldet.
Wobei Sammelklage nur ein Hilfsbegriff ist. Genau genommen muss jede Frau selbst ein Schlichtungsverfahren bei der Stadt einleiten. Wird sie dort, wie auch Gradik Ende Juni, abgewiesen, ist der Weg für eine Klage offen.
Internationales Medienecho
Die Aussicht auf Erfolg dürfte nicht so schlecht stehen. „Frauen dürfen nicht allein deshalb finanziell benachteiligt werden, weil sie eine andere Anatomie haben und auch aus Sicherheitsgründen auf eine Kabine angewiesen sind“, sagte etwa die Rechtsprofessorin Anna Gamper von der Universität Innsbruck der französischen Nachrichtenagentur AFP.
Denn der Fall sorgt mittlerweile auch international für Aufmerksamkeit. Mit so einem Medienecho hat Gradik jedenfalls nicht gerechnet. Es wirkt ohnehin, als wäre die 27-Jährige eher zufällig in die Sache hineingerutscht, ohne großen Plan. Sie macht es einfach, weil sie wütend ist. „Das ist doch nur ein weiteres Beispiel dafür, wie wir Frauen im Alltag diskriminiert werden. Männer gehen sorglos durch die Welt, pinkeln irgendwo hin, und ihnen passiert nichts.“
Gründe: Sauberkeit, Vandalismus, Wasserverbrauch
Im Koalitionsprogramm der rot-pinken Stadtregierung hat man versprochen, vollständig kostenlose Toiletten zu „prüfen“. Gründe, warum die Stadt bisher nichts geändert hat, gibt es aber einige. Die Gebühr sei nötig, um an stark frequentierten Orten durch Toilettenpersonal Sauberkeit und die ordnungsgemäße Nutzung sicherstellen zu können, heißt es etwa. Oder um Vandalismus vorzubeugen. Mitunter wurde auch der höhere Wasserverbrauch bei den Kloschüsseln ins Treffen geführt. Zudem kostet die Errichtung der Toiletten selbst einiges: Für eine moderne Toilettenanlage sind das bis zu einer halben Million Euro.
Im Vergleich dazu wirken die 1000 Euro, die die Stadt im Falle einer Niederlage vor Gericht an Gradik zahlen muss, und die diese an ein Frauenhaus spenden will, geradezu lächerlich. Sofern sich nicht noch viel mehr Frauen dem WC-Kampf anschließen.
Auf einen Blick
167 öffentliche WC-Anlagen gibt es in Wien. Die meisten sind kostenlos, bei 27 Anlagen kostet die Nutzung der Kabine 50 Cent, die Pissoirs sind gratis zugänglich. Die 27-jährige Melanie Gradik hält das für Diskriminierung und zieht gegen die Stadt Wien vor Gericht.
Sie und ihre Anwältin rufen andere Frauen auf, sich einer Sammelklage anzuschließen, unter www.50cent.at
Mindestens 1000 Euro Schadensersatz sieht das Wiener Antidiskriminierungsgesetz pro betroffener Person, die Recht behält, vor.

title: US judge strikes down policy suspending immigrant visa processing for 75 nations
content:
U.S. District Judge Jeannette Vargas in Manhattan said the policy that the State Department announced in January was "patently unlawful" and ran afoul of federal immigration law, which explicitly stripped the secretary of state of authority over consular officers' processing of immigrant visas.
"The Policy, which categorically prohibits the issuance of immigrant visas based upon the nationality of the applicant, represents a direct abrogation of this statutory scheme," she wrote.
The State Department's suspension that also took effect in January impacted applicants from Latin American countries including Brazil, Colombia, and Uruguay; Balkan nations such as Bosnia and Albania; South Asian countries Pakistan and Bangladesh; and those from many nations in Africa, the Middle East, and the Caribbean.
The State Department said applicants from those countries were "at a high risk for becoming a public charge and recourse to local, state and federal government resources in the United States." The department did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the ruling.
Vargas, an appointee of Democratic former President Joe Biden, issued the ruling in a lawsuit filed by immigrant rights groups Catholic Legal Immigration Network and African Communities Together along with applicants for immigrant visas and U.S. citizens who are sponsoring family members from the designated countries for immigrant visas.
President Donald Trump has pursued an aggressive immigration crackdown that he says is aimed at improving domestic security.
Rights groups say the crackdown has violated free speech and due process rights and has created an unsafe environment, particularly for ethnic minorities, who have raised concerns about racial profiling.

title: Nuclear power plants unaffected by earthquake off southwest coast: authorities
content:
Nuclear power plants unaffected by earthquake off southwest coast: authorities
SEOUL, Aug. 23 (Yonhap) -- All nuclear power plants in South Korea are operating normally without being affected by a magnitude 3.1 earthquake that struck off the southwestern coast Sunday, authorities said.
The quake was detected 21 kilometers west of the southwestern county of Haenam at 6:43 a.m. and the seismic readings at all nuclear plants fell short of the minimum needed to trigger an alarm, according to the state-run Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power Co.
The Nuclear Safety and Security Commission also said no safety issues arose at any nuclear reactor facility. The Hanbit Nuclear Power Plant, the closest to the earthquake's epicenter at a distance of approximately 83 km, had a seismic reading of 0.0032g, far below its seismic design standard of 0.2g, it said.

title: I was spending £700 a month: How I beat my late-night shopping addiction
content:
I was spending £700 a month: How I beat my late-night shopping addiction
- Published
You may well have been there. It's late, you're scrolling on your phone and suddenly feel a strong urge to buy something - only to wake up the next day and regret it.
But what happens when those impulse buys become a habit rather than a one-off?
One global study suggests 7% of adults, external experience shopping addiction, external - an uncontrollable urge to spend despite the financial consequences - and younger women are more susceptible.
Ella Hewitt, from Liverpool, says her shopping addiction got so bad in 2021 that she was spending up to £700 a month on fast fashion she couldn't afford and sometimes never even wore.
"I didn't grow up with much money, so when I got a job I would spend my wages as soon as they hit my account," says the 24-year-old.
"That dopamine hit kept me shopping and in the world of social media there is just so much encouragement to do that."
She says she would often make purchases on TikTok or Instagram when she was "tired" or "bored", lured by the latest trends on her feeds.
She was working as an HR assistant in a school at the time and her spending meant she couldn't afford to move out of her family home.
"Horrified" by how much she was buying, she began using diversionary tactics to control her spending.
One was to put anything she felt like buying on a wish list and wait 30 days.
"If I still wanted it, I would buy it, but more often than not I'd find the urge had gone," she says.
'I'm way more in control'
Ella gave herself an imaginary budget of £1,000 each day to spend on imaginary purchases, which "scratched the itch" of shopping without the cost.
And she vowed only to buy something if she could afford to "buy it three times".
"Overall, I cut my spending by about 60%," says Ella, who now works as an ethical fashion influencer and plans to launch her own clothing brand.
"I'm not perfect. There are times when I will buy things because I want it. But I am way more in control."
The Ukat Group, which runs addiction treatment centres across the country, says it has seen more people with a shopping addiction and 90% are women.
It says there are various signs you may have a , externalproblem, external, such as your mood improving immediately after making a purchase, or feeling guilty or ashamed afterwards.
You may also lie to loved ones about your spending habit or have a home "full of items you don't need or use".
Tips to get your spending under control
- Wait 48 hours or longer before you purchase something. Often the urge will go
- Delete saved credit card numbers and shopping apps
- Write a shopping list before you enter a store or visit a site, and stick to it
- Set a small budget for guilt-free treats, or create an imaginary one
- Unsubscribe from retailer newsletters and alerts and unfollow influencers
- Use up products before buying new ones; accessorise rather than buying brand new outfits.
- Know your triggers: If you shop when you feel lonely, bored or stressed, try exercise or talking with a friend instead
- Seek help: Citizens Advice, Stepchange, Christians Against Poverty and National Debtline can all offer advice on money problems.
Sources: The United Nations Federal Credit Union, Christians Against Poverty
'I would buy anything that was trending'
Dish Patel, 23, from London, says she was spending so much on clothes, food, make-up and skincare as a student that she "maxed out" her £2,500 overdraft and was "always broke".
Like Ella, she thinks she was making up for not having much money as a child, but the joy was always short-lived.
"The feeling you get when you open your new parcels is always amazing until the dopamine hit dies down and the cycle repeats."
Dish, who now works as a financial planner, says she would buy "pretty much anything that was trending" but her biggest vice was scrolling on shopping apps to pass the time.
'I didn't want to spend the money twice'
Then, she deleted shopping apps like Asos and Pretty Little Thing from her phone and removed ApplePay to make it harder to buy things in a single click.
She even started leaving her bank cards at home when she went to work.
"I would bring a packed lunch in and I would buy my train ticket on Trainline the night before... This basically put me in a habit of not spending a single thing and pre-planning my day to ensure I don't spend anything."
She also vowed that any time she wanted to buy something, she had to put the same amount of money into her savings or investments.
"It worked because I didn't want to spend the money twice."
Research last year from Vanquis, a challenger bank, found Gen Z shoppers make more impulse purchases than any other age group, external, closely followed by millennials.
And some experts say exposure to social media, with its targeted advertising, influencer culture and seamless one-click checkout, is fuelling the trend, external.
Money and Mental Health, a charity, also blames the design of online shopping sites for "minimising the friction around spending money".
It points to "pop-ups" that put customers under pressure to spend, and the inclusion of alternative payment methods like Buy Now Pay Later.
The BBC has contacted Meta, which owns Instagram, TikTok and Asos for comment.

title: Akylman Presidential Lyceum to open in Manas in September
content:
The Akylman Presidential Lyceum in Manas is scheduled to open in September, at the start of the new academic year. The Ministry of Construction, Architecture, Housing and Communal Services of Kyrgyzstan reported.
The lyceum is designed for 360 students. The project includes a 410-bed dormitory, accommodation for teachers, laboratories, a library, a 25-meter swimming pool, a sports hall and a stadium.
Initially, the estimated cost of the project exceeded 2.1 billion soms, while the construction cost per square meter was estimated at $1,103.
Following a revision of the project, the cost per square meter was reduced to $750, while the total estimated cost was cut to 1.7 billion soms. According to the ministry, this resulted in savings of 443.5 million soms.
Construction and installation work at the site is currently nearing completion.
- The Akylman Presidential Lyceum was established in 2023 to provide education for gifted children from across Kyrgyzstan. The first such institution opened in Cholpon-Ata. Tuition, accommodation and meals are provided free of charge, with admission based on a competitive selection process.
- Starting from the new academic year, branches of the lyceum are expected to begin operating in Manas and Talas.

title: Civil rights groups make urgent plea for voting rights
content:
Civil rights groups make urgent plea for voting rights
Thousands of protesters are rallying on the National Mall in support of voting rights and racial justice ahead of the midterm election
WASHINGTON -- Thousands of protesters are rallying Friday on the National Mall in support of voting rights and racial justice ahead of the midterm elections, following a wave of changes to voting laws and redistricting that civil rights groups have condemned as detrimental to Black Americans.
The 2026 “Defend the Vote” March on Washington, organized by the Rev. Al Sharpton and Martin Luther King III, echoes the Rev. Martin Luther King Jr.'s 1963 march. The event follows the U.S. Supreme Court’s landmark April decision in Louisiana v. Callais that reinterpreted key provisions of the Voting Rights Act of 1965, allowing Southern states to redraw their congressional maps in a way that erodes equal representation in Black communities.
“We’ve been doing these marches for years, but this is probably the most important because this is the first year we are marching that the voting rights bill has been nullified by the Supreme Court,” Sharpton, founder of the National Action Network, said in an interview with The Associated Press.
“Marches are designed to grab attention and then go into the trenches and organize around that,” he said.
The march opened with prayer and statements from Interfaith Alliance representatives. They spoke on diversity, equity and inclusion practices, voting rights and systemic racism.
“Creator of all, let us draw on each other, with love and mercy, and hold each other up as we march, wipe each other’s tears, heal each other’s wounds,” Ambereen Kahn, an Interfaith Alliance representative, said. “Most compassionate, protect our leaders who guide, instill in their hearts the values of our shared humanity.”
This year’s march, which Sharpton's group is co-hosting with King's Drum Major Institute, a progressive think tank and community action group, features dozens of speakers, including Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y.
Sharpton said thousands of civil rights activists from across the southeastern U.S. were traveling to the capital by bus for the rally.
On Thursday, Courtney Pope, 48, was marching across the King Bridge to the Civil Rights Museum in Memphis. But on Friday, she and other members of the National Handmaid Army were at the Washington march with plans to travel to New York and New Jersey over the next few days.
For Pope, the rally is about finding community alongside promoting voting rights.
“I know that we’ll only be successful if we band together despite our differences,” Pope said.
Friday's event harkens back to King Jr.’s historic March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom in 1963, when more than 200,000 people gathered at the foot of the Lincoln Memorial. That march, an inflection point in the Civil Rights Movement, came at a fraught moment for the country, when economic headwinds, civil unrest, political division and the Vietnam War bitterly divided Americans.
Sharpton said the Trump administration’s immigration policy for Haitians and white South Africans, as well as cuts to social programs like Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act’s health subsidies, are unifying policies for this year's ideologically diverse march attendees. But the redistricting efforts by Republican-led states set to reduce the number of Black lawmakers in Congress loom large over Friday's march.
“This march is about people who refuse to be counted out. When the courts and the legislature broke apart District 6, they did not just redraw lines,” Rep. Cleo Fields, D-La., said in a texted statement. “They told hundreds of thousands of Black families from Baton Rouge up through the Delta that their voice could be taken away at any moment.”
Fields was the central character in the Supreme Court decision that hollowed out the Voting Rights Act of 1965. The court ruled that his district, created just one term ago to permit a second majority-Black district in a state where Blacks make up 33% of the population, was unconstitutional because it relied too heavily on race.
The court has held that maps can be redrawn for partisan reasons.
Louisiana's legislature rushed to redraw the district after the high court's decision, reshaping Fields’ district to cluster it around predominantly white communities in the Baton Rouge area and southern Louisiana.
Fields has opted not to seek reelection to Congress and instead is pursuing a seat in the state Senate.
“The people taking part in this historic march are answering back, and history will remember that they did,” Fields said.
Rep. Shomari Figures, an Alabama Democrat whose majority-Black district was targeted by the state’s Republican-led redistricting effort, said the original voting rights fight required local movements, national figures, lots of coordination and strategy. He sees this year's march as a continuation of that legacy.
“My district includes Montgomery, which was the birthplace of it all. It started with a bus boycott in 1955 and that, ultimately, morphed into a broader struggle for civil rights and led to a more broad Civil Rights Movement,” Figures told the AP.
“It led to a Civil Rights Act, led to the Fair Housing Act, led obviously to the Voting Rights Act, and the voting rights movement,” Figures added.
Ahead of Friday, organizations participating in the march, including the NAACP, the Lawyers’ Committee for Civil Rights Under Law, and Black Voters Matter, filed new claims in federal court in their existing lawsuit against President Donald Trump's executive order restricting mail-in voting. The Supreme Court cleared a path Monday for possible implementation of the order, though it remains unclear how much can be put in place before the midterms.
“We will not stand idly by while the voices of the people are silenced,” NAACP President Derrick Johnson said in a statement Thursday. “We must protect every eligible citizen’s right to cast their ballot.”
____
Associated Press writers Gary Fields in Washington and Kimberly Chandler in Montgomery, Alabama, contributed.

title: More UK businesses increasing investment in heat adaptation, survey finds
content:
The mercury climbed. Many companies noticed. More than a third of UK firms have already sunk capital into surviving extreme temperatures.
Cooling equipment is the obvious priority. But the response goes further. Some are rethinking how and when their staff work. Others are eyeing energy efficiency. Yet the financial impact is uneven, with small businesses faring worse than their larger rivals.
We examine which sectors are adapting, and why the climate crisis is no longer a distant threat but an immediate operational concern.

In response to the record-breaking heatwaves experienced across the country, 37% of UK businesses have invested in heat adaptation, with a further 23% considering doing so, according to the survey.
The bank stated that the most common priority was upgrading cooling equipment such as air conditioning and ventilation, with 28% of businesses investing in this. Another 23% said they were adopting energy efficiency measures to lower their energy use.
According to Barclays’ data, this rising interest in cooling saw air conditioning suppliers increase their cash inflows into Barclays accounts by 4.3% year-on-year.
Beyond investment in physical interventions, almost 30% of businesses also said they had introduced other wellbeing measures, including 23% that said they had offered flexible or remote working and 21% that adjusted working hours.
In response to this year’s heatwaves, Green MP Hannah Spencer proposed legislation that would pave the way for maximum workplace temperatures in the UK.
The bill would establish an independent body to recommend maximum safe workplace temperatures and advise on how those recommendations should be implemented.
The Health and Safety Executive has previously said it does not support a single maximum workplace temperature because excessive heat can result from workplace activities as well as weather conditions.
Although there is no legal minimum workplace temperature, the guidance recommends 16C for most workplaces and 13C where work involves significant physical effort.
The Barclays survey also found that businesses were not impacted equally; 27% of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) reported that the hot weather had harmed their productivity, while 47% of large businesses reported a boost in productivity.
Related article: ONS: Heat linked to more than 40,000 deaths in England since 1988
Consumer spending
In addition to impacting business operations and internal investment patterns, Barclays’ recent UK Consumer Spends Report also noted that the hot weather had changed demand and trading conditions for businesses, in particular retailers.
Spending across all retail grew 2.1% in July, with face-to-face retail also up 1.4% from June. This included increased spending across clothing, gardening, and electronics, with almost a quarter of people reporting having bought some kind of cooling device.
Almost 40% of people also said they had bought cold food and drinks in July to cope with the soaring temperatures.

title: Natural forest regrowth offers a lower-cost path to climate and biodiversity goals
content:
As nations race to restore ecosystems and curb climate change, research has shown that letting nature do the work is a cost-effective, viable solution. A study from the University of Queensland and the University of Newcastle found that natural forest regeneration delivered substantial carbon and biodiversity benefits and could be up to 96% cheaper than traditional tree-planting programs. The work is published in the journal Nature Ecology & Evolution.
School of the Environment Ph.D. candidate Jiaqi Li said the team mapped how the costs and benefits of natural regeneration varied across the tropics.
"Nature is a great gardener. Sometimes we just need to get out of its way while providing a bit of support," Li said.
"For tree planting, you need to purchase seeds and hire workers or recruit volunteers to plant and manage them, which is costly.
"For natural regeneration, people just need to check the land for invasive species and remove them, make sure there are adequate seed sources, provide protection from fire, grazing animals and humans, and then it is mostly self-sufficient.
"In many cases of natural regeneration, studies show that you can end up with a forest that could store more carbon and is more biodiverse than a planted forest."
Forests recover at lower cost
Between 2000 and 2012, tropical forests were reduced globally by 2.3 million km² (890,000 square miles), leading to the release of an estimated 0.86 gigatons of carbon annually and threatening the well-being of around 1.5 billion people dependent on forests.
"Forests are Earth's life-support systems, and tropical forests are the most biodiverse among all forest types, covering 18% of the land and home to more than half of all land vertebrate species," Li said.
"They are also a giant carbon sink, so when deforestation happens, we not only stop the forest from taking up carbon, but we also flip it and turn it into a carbon source."
Where the strongest gains appear
Li said the study identified areas where natural regeneration provided high carbon benefits, high biodiversity benefits and low restoration costs and called them "holistic hotspots."
These areas were mostly located in Indonesia, Madagascar, the Philippines, Mexico and Malaysia.
"The carbon benefits stand out most in Neotropical areas like the Amazon basin and in the Indomalayan tropics like Borneo, Sumatra and Papua New Guinea," Li said.
"There are more biodiversity benefits in the Afrotropics, including Madagascar."
Restoration goals meet budget limits
Senior author Dr. Brooke Williams from the University of Newcastle said that, with the world pledging in the 2022 Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework to restore 30% of Earth's degraded land, natural regeneration was more important than ever.
"The whole world is fighting climate change, and on top of that, nations have goals to reverse the biodiversity crisis," Williams said.
"Restoring forests is expensive, and the cost could mean some nations can't meet their ambitious restoration goals.
"Our study gives a broad idea of the benefits and costs that could occur with natural regeneration."
Turning restoration theory into action
UQ Associate Professor Matthew Luskin, who co-authored the study, said the research was a huge leap forward in putting theories about forest restoration into practice.
"I've spent years in forests around the tropics and seen rampant deforestation firsthand, but I've also seen huge opportunities for regrowth," Luskin said.
"This work will help countries and communities prioritize where and how to invest in restoration depending on their specific goals and resources to achieve the best outcomes."
